title: Indian-Origin NYC Mayor Mamdani Faces Backlash After Suspected Hate Crime Stabbings
excerpt: Two men — one Asian, one Jewish — were stabbed near Central Park on Thursday after the suspect allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar," thrusting Mayor Zohran Mamdani into a political firestorm over his response and rhetoric on Israel.
body:
• Suspect Raul Morales, 51, allegedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" while stabbing a 57-year-old Asian man and a 50-year-old Jewish man on Manhattan's Upper West Side
  • Both victims are in stable condition and expected to survive; NYPD is investigating the attacks as a potential hate crime
  • Jewish community leaders directly blamed Indian-origin Mayor Zohran Mamdani's anti-Israel rhetoric for fostering a climate of violence against Jews
  • Mamdani was criticized for a delayed public response before calling the attacks "hateful and despicable"

Two men were stabbed in broad daylight on Manhattan's Upper West Side on Thursday afternoon in what police are evaluating as a potential hate crime — an attack that has thrust Indian-origin New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani into a deepening political crisis over antisemitism and his stance on Israel.

Raul Morales, 51, allegedly attacked a 57-year-old Asian man near West 84th Street and Central Park West shortly after 1:30 p.m., then stabbed a 50-year-old Jewish man blocks away near West 86th Street and Amsterdam Avenue, according to the NYPD. The Jewish victim had just left a nearby synagogue before being attacked, a rabbi at the Jewish center confirmed to Fox 5 NY.

Witness and victim statements report Morales yelled "Allahu Akbar" during both attacks, Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said. A witness also observed him walking erratically and shouting incoherently — including yelling the word "Islam" — on Columbus Avenue roughly half an hour later, according to the New York Post.

"I saw a man kneeling on the street with a knife just sticking out of his back, like a movie."

— Marianna Ellenberg, witness, speaking to CNN

Both victims were transported to Mount Sinai Morningside in stable condition and are expected to survive. A knife and screwdriver were recovered following Morales's arrest at 89th Street and Amsterdam Avenue. A UPS delivery driver followed the suspect and led officers to his hiding location, according to People.

Hate Crime Investigation

The NYPD's hate crime task force is investigating Morales's motive. Tisch noted that while he has no known mental health history with the department, "the initial investigation suggests that mental health may have been a factor." He had not been formally charged as of Friday morning. Public records show two prior drug-possession arrests from 1991.

https://x.com/Bubblebathgirl/status/2080473123049152581

There is no known connection between Morales and either victim, or between the two victims, police said. The attacks were unprovoked, according to CNN.

Jewish Leaders Blast Mamdani

The stabbings have intensified scrutiny of Mamdani, a Democratic socialist who has faced sustained criticism over his vocal opposition to the Israeli government. Jewish community leaders held a press conference near the scene Friday morning, directly linking the violence to the mayor's rhetoric.

"When the mayor of New York repeatedly uses his platform to relentlessly single out and demonize Israel, the world's only Jewish state, and calls those who support it 'monsters,' he contributes to a climate in which Jewish New Yorkers are increasingly targeted and unsafe."

— Eric Goldstein, CEO, UJA-Federation of New York

"Mayor Mamdani, stop fanning the flames of hatred and division. The consequences are not abstract; they are playing out on our streets," Goldstein added. Mark Treyger, CEO of the Jewish Community Relations Council, called for the Manhattan District Attorney's Office "to fully prosecute this to the fullest extent of the law."

City Council member Inna Vernikov went further, writing on social media: "Mamdani, you got blood on your hands."

Mamdani's Delayed Response

Mamdani drew criticism for remaining silent on the stabbings for several hours, instead posting about his millionaire housing tax initiative, according to Fox News. When he did respond, he called the attacks "hateful and despicable."

"The NYPD responded immediately and arrested Raul Morales in connection with both assaults — and I am grateful to the officers for their swift response," Mamdani wrote on X.

Governor Kathy Hochul was more direct in her condemnation, saying she was "disgusted by what appears to be another senseless attack on New Yorkers simply because they're Jewish." City Council Speaker Julie Menin called the attack "abhorrent," adding that "the fear in the Jewish community is real."

A Diaspora Milestone Under Strain

Mamdani, of Indian and Ugandan descent, made history as New York City's first mayor of South Asian origin — a milestone celebrated across the Indian diaspora. But his progressive politics, particularly his criticism of Israel, have placed him at the center of one of American politics' most volatile fault lines. He recently explored whether Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu could be arrested during a visit to New York under the International Criminal Court warrant issued in 2024, according to the Wall Street Journal.

What's Next

The outcome of the NYPD's hate crime investigation — and whether Morales faces formal hate crime charges — will be closely watched. For Mamdani, the political fallout may prove equally consequential, as Jewish organizations signal they will continue pressing his administration on what they call a deteriorating climate of safety for Jewish New Yorkers.
nri_angle: Indian-origin NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani faces intense political backlash from Jewish community leaders who blame his anti-Israel rhetoric for fostering a climate of violence, after two men were stabbed in a suspected hate crime on the Upper West Side.
author: Diaspora Desk
